articles.title: Five for Accel: Mossdeep turns a tied game into 63–10
articles.dek: Accel BeckhmJr caught five touchdowns and Dram Marino threw six as the unbeaten Eclipse overwhelmed Lavender before their bye.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: Lavender had its answer ready. Mossdeep scored, Mr. Clanky took the kickoff back 100 yards, and for a few minutes the Wails had turned the league's most productive offense into one half of a tied game. That was the last time the afternoon belonged to both teams. The Eclipse scored the next 21 points before halftime and finished a 63–10 victory with Accel BeckhmJr collecting five receiving touchdowns.

Eight catches. Ten targets. Two hundred and thirty-three yards. BeckhmJr needed all of one touchdown to put Mossdeep ahead 28–7 before the break, then added four more in a second-half stretch that made every Lavender possession feel urgently short. The Eclipse are 7–0, have scored 307 points and will spend Week 8 on a bye. The Wails are 4–2 and have Blackthorn next. Travis Scarboro has a very different week to prepare.
I was going to count them on one hand, then remembered the ball was still coming. Dram made the hard part look suspiciously easy. Ask him about that.
body.speaker: Accel BeckhmJr

body.text: Dram Marino's contribution was substantial enough to survive the joke. The Drampa completed 22 of 28 passes for 381 yards, six touchdowns and no interceptions. He found eight different receivers. Gronkaludon caught all five of his targets for 43 yards, and Marshall Flock turned his only reception into a 12-yard touchdown. Mossdeep's quarterback now has 22 passing scores against two interceptions through seven games. Michael Dorrill's attack is giving defenses several problems before the most spectacular one arrives.
A tie that did not last

Ninjaskamara opened the scoring on a ten-yard run left with 3:33 remaining in the first quarter. Adam Vinathorn converted, then kicked off to Mr. Clanky. The Iron Bundle returned it 100 yards for Lavender's only touchdown; the extra point made it 7–7. It was an enormous special-teams response from a player whose passing afternoon would become increasingly difficult.

Lavender could not turn that burst into sustained offense. Mr. Clanky finished 12 of 34 for 102 yards with two interceptions. The Wails produced eight first downs and 161 total yards. Mossdeep finished with 18 and 531. A return touchdown counts every bit as much as a long offensive drive, but it does not solve the next third down, and the Wails converted only four of eleven.

Ninjaskamara scored again with 5:18 left in the second quarter, taking a seven-yard run left into the end zone. Marino later threw deep right to Flock for the 12-yard score with 2:06 remaining. Mossdeep was moving the ball with a lead, a running threat and several passing destinations available. Lavender was already being asked to create another exceptional response.

The Wails did make Marino uncomfortable on individual snaps. Grimace Shake sacked him twice, including a six-yard loss with 39 seconds left before halftime. That brought up third-and-eleven. Marino immediately answered with a short-left throw to BeckhmJr for a 14-yard touchdown at 0:21. A defensive success had created the down Lavender wanted. The next play still ended in the end zone.
After the sack, the distance was the thing to settle. Accel gave me a throw I could finish. I don't want the six touchdowns to hide how many ordinary catches kept us moving.
body.speaker: Dram Marino

body.text: Four scores, both sides of the field

Lavender's 29-yard field goal with 3:38 remaining in the third quarter brought the score to 28–10. Ninjaskamara answered later with his third rushing touchdown, a four-yard run up the middle at 0:34. His final rushing line was 19 carries for 90 yards; he also caught a 39-yard pass. A minor injury appears in the game report, with no remaining absence listed in the current injury report.

Then the takeaways and BeckhmJr's routes began arriving together. Derrat Brooks intercepted a deep-right throw with 17 seconds left in the third and returned it 14 yards. Six seconds later, Marino threw deep right to BeckhmJr for a 35-yard touchdown. Mossdeep took a 42–10 lead into the fourth quarter, and Lavender's attempts to chase the game were now handing the Eclipse additional chances.

BeckhmJr scored from 39 yards on a short-left pass at 5:14. Clay Rathews intercepted Mr. Clanky's next deep-right attempt at 4:55, returning it 18 yards. At 4:30, Marino went deep right to BeckhmJr for a 30-yard touchdown. At 4:03, they connected deep left for 55 more. Three fourth-quarter scores, in a span of 71 seconds on the game clock, took a rout to 63 points.

Those descriptions matter. BeckhmJr's touchdowns were not all deep throws and they did not all attack the same side. Short left produced scores of 14 and 39 yards; deep right produced 35 and 30; deep left supplied 55. The receiving totals show the damage. The sequence shows why Lavender never found a comfortable place to defend it.
The work beneath the headline

Mossdeep converted eight of ten third downs and punted once. Flock added 42 rushing yards on five carries to his touchdown catch. Gronkaludon's five receptions and the catches by Travis Meltce, Lorenzo Steel and Ninjulio Jones kept Marino's distribution wider than the five-touchdown headline suggests. Vinathorn made all nine extra points. There was very little wasted finishing work.

The defense forced two interceptions and broke up ten passes in the team comparison. Shawn Mareman, the defensive player of the game, had a sack, a pass defended and six pressures in his individual line. Luvrelle Revis recorded three passes defended. The Wails' best offensive receiving total belonged to Beedrill, with three catches for 39 yards. Mr. Clanky's return was remarkable; Lavender needed far more of the possessions after it.

For Scarboro, the next opponent offers no gentle reset. Blackthorn just beat Lavaridge 42–0 and sits 5–1. Lavender remains in the playoff picture, but its record now comes with 78 points scored and 130 allowed. The response has to begin with possessions that let its defense rest and a passing game that can survive without a return touchdown doing the scoring.

Mossdeep gets a week without a game and a receiver whose season totals have jumped to 24 catches, 568 yards and ten touchdowns. Half those touchdowns came here. The last was the 55-yarder to the left, after Lavender had already been hurt to the right and underneath. By then, BeckhmJr had run out of new ways to count them.

art.alt: Accel BeckhmJr, Accelgor No. 11, with a football in Mossdeep magenta and gold.

articles.title: Four kicks, then four incompletions: Cerulean makes twelve enough
articles.dek: Grotle supplied every Tide point. The defense finished a 12–6 upset by denying Sunyshore four straight throws on its final possession.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Cerulean won the part of this game that happened after Sunyshore seemed to have found its answer. Three consecutive completions moved the Starseekers 53 yards on their final possession. Then came four incompletions, two broken up by Carnivine and one by Maractus. A 12–6 win required all four stops. The Tide made them, and Grotle’s four field goals suddenly looked like a sufficient offensive plan.

Sunyshore had scored first, on DeZhaun Watzon’s one-yard run up the middle with 2:10 remaining in the opening quarter. The extra point missed. That single touchdown stood as the Starseekers’ entire scoring return, despite two late possessions that could have changed the result. Karson Jones’s team fell to 5–2. Cerulean improved to 4–3, with a win that will make its bye week rather easier to enjoy.

The useful distinction is how each passing game handled the ordinary work. Farigiraf completed 23 of 37 throws for 197 yards without an interception or a sack. Watzon finished 10-for-26 for 125, threw an interception and took three sacks. Neither quarterback threw a touchdown. One gave his kicker enough opportunities to score four times; the other spent much of the afternoon trying to recover from possessions that had gone nowhere.
Four is a nice number when all four go through. I wasn’t standing there wishing we needed a more interesting kick. Twenty-four yards suits me fine.
body.speaker: Grotle

body.text: Grotle began with a 25-yarder at the opening of the second quarter, finishing a possession that had covered 59 yards. His 40-yarder with 1:54 left in the half tied the game at six. A 36-yarder with two seconds remaining put Cerulean ahead. The fourth, from 24 yards with 1:48 left in the third, set the final margin. There was no long-distance rescue here. Cerulean repeatedly brought him into usable range, and he finished every assignment.
The interception bought three points

The second kick followed Vikavolt’s interception of Watzon’s deep-right pass at 3:04 in the second quarter. Vikavolt returned it 21 yards. Cerulean then gained 16 yards on the ensuing possession before Grotle tied the score. That is a modest amount of offense, but a meaningful exchange in a game where every scoring chance mattered. Sunyshore had given the Tide a shorter route to three points.

Pressure supplied a different form of disruption. Watchog sacked Watzon for a six-yard loss in the second quarter. Chesnaught added losses of eight and five in the third. Cerulean recorded three sacks while allowing none. The difference did not produce a spectacular defensive touchdown; it helped make an afternoon of unsuccessful drives possible. Sunyshore converted two of nine third downs and punted five times.

The Tide were hardly strolling down the field themselves. They ran 21 times for only 28 yards and also punted five times. Seismitoad’s eleven carries produced seventeen yards. The answer came through short gains in the passing game: Arctozolt caught six of seven targets for 57 yards, Delcatty added six catches for 49, and Watchog caught four for 40. Cerulean converted six of sixteen third downs. It needed persistence because explosive offense was in short supply.

For Misty, that balance was enough to create four scoring possessions without asking the running game to become something it was not. The Tide finished with 225 yards to Sunyshore’s 207. The eighteen-yard gap was small; the difference in wasted opportunities was larger. Cerulean lost no fumbles and threw no interceptions. Sunyshore lost one of each.
Two chances, two different failures

The fumble arrived late enough to look decisive. With 2:03 remaining in the fourth quarter, Scol Alexander ran left for a two-yard loss and lost the ball. Shellder recovered for Cerulean. Sunyshore had moved 57 yards on that possession before it ended. A team chasing six points cannot assume the next chance will arrive after giving one away so close to the finish.

It did arrive. Cerulean could not drain the game, and Grotle punted with 1:54 left. Watzon hit Floatzel short right for six yards, then Sceptile short right for 21, then Floatzel deep left for 26. Those three throws briefly supplied exactly the passing rhythm missing for most of the afternoon. Sunyshore was threatening again, with enough time to complete the task.

The final four throws went to four successive situations with the same result. Carnivine broke up attempts to MF STOMP short right and deep right. Maractus denied a deep-left pass to FIN FANG FOOM. On fourth-and-ten, the short-right attempt to Frigibax fell incomplete with 1:09 remaining. Farigiraf took over for two kneels. Cerulean had survived the recovery from its own failure to close the game a possession earlier.
We found three good throws, and then I needed another one. It’s a very small number until the whole game is asking you for it.
body.speaker: DeZhaun Watzon

body.text: The game’s injury list marked Myles Gabite and Scol Alexander with minor issues. Neither entry supplies an explanation for the sequence of missed chances, and neither should replace the visible football. Sunyshore gets Mahogany next. The immediate repair is straightforward to describe and harder to perform: more completed throws before the final possession, fewer lost opportunities after a drive has begun to work.

Cerulean can carry a simpler memory into its bye. Its offense did not reach the end zone, its defense did not surrender a point after the first quarter, and its kicker missed nothing. When the lead was finally tested by three sharp completions, Carnivine and Maractus put their hands on the answer.

art.alt: Cerulean kicker Grotle No. 3 beside a football on a tee.

articles.title: Porygon-Z finds the second-half answer for unbeaten Mt. Silver
articles.dek: Porygon-Z threw two second-half touchdowns, Tony Gyarzalez reached 100 yards, and Mt. Silver rallied past Petalburg 17–14 to reach 7–0.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Mt. Silver’s seventh win required a scoreless first half, a long throw to a familiar tight end, and a quarterback who finished with the ball from an onside kick. Porygon-Z wore No. 8 and supplied the full passing line: 21 completions on 33 attempts, 223 yards and two touchdowns. The Reds beat Petalburg 17–14. Their record stayed perfect while their season continued to change around it.

A week ago, Crem Ftzpatrik’s relief appearance had become the immediate answer after Josh Alakazam was lost for the season. This game belonged to Porygon-Z. There is no need to make the transition more mysterious or more tidy than the football itself. Connor McLarren needed a productive afternoon from the quarterback on the field. He got one, eventually, after Petalburg had spent an entire half making the new assignment uncomfortable.

The Pride led 7–0 at halftime. Iron Valiant had found Golbat short left for a six-yard touchdown with 1:54 left in the first quarter, and Petalburg’s defense protected that lead through a second quarter in which neither team scored. Delcatty sacked Porygon-Z twice before the break. A 76-yard Reds possession ended on downs. Mt. Silver had movement, but no points to show for it.
Tony kept giving me somewhere useful to throw it. I’m happy to let everybody admire the hundred yards. I was mostly pleased he kept being available.
body.speaker: Porygon-Z

body.text: Tony Gyarzalez finished with five catches for 100 yards. The one that changed the shape of the afternoon arrived early in the third quarter: third-and-ten, 5:50 on the clock, a deep-right pass that went for 59 yards. After a half spent assembling gains without a scoring finish, the Reds had crossed a large piece of the field in one throw. Flygon made the tackle, leaving Mt. Silver more work to do.
Seventeen points after the break

Petalburg still resisted. Delcatty recorded a third sack, again for seven yards, with 4:44 left in the third quarter. The Reds eventually settled for Adam Venutieri’s 28-yard field goal at 4:21. It cut the lead to 7–3. That was a successful defensive stand after the long completion, but it was also the first time Mt. Silver had received any payment for its offensive work.

The next scoring possession finished differently. Porygon-Z found Gregar Jenings short left for eight yards on third-and-eight with 1:01 remaining in the third. The touchdown and extra point made it 10–7. On a later drive in the fourth, Scep Smith Jr. caught a three-yard touchdown, again on a short-left throw, with 3:55 left. The Reds had scored seventeen unanswered points, using the long completion to begin the recovery and shorter throws to finish it.

Gyarzalez did not score. Plusico Buress did not score either, though his six catches for 45 yards supplied a substantial part of the ordinary work between the larger moments. The pair accounted for eleven of Porygon-Z’s 21 completions. I tend to trust that kind of distribution more than a story in which a new quarterback supposedly becomes self-sufficient overnight. There were useful receivers accepting their share of the afternoon.
The long one helped us. So did the next short catch. When we were behind, I wanted us to keep seeing the whole field and the whole game. There was still time.
body.speaker: Tony Gyarzalez

body.text: Raticate carried nine times for 48 yards, and Vibrava added 43 on six attempts. Mt. Silver finished with 89 rushing yards, including the two late kneels that reduced the total. With Garshawn Lynch still out, the supporting runners again supplied enough movement to keep the offense from becoming entirely about its quarterback. That is a continuing responsibility, not a one-game favor.

Petalburg’s offense had its own productive runner. Oinkologne gained 62 yards on eleven carries and caught both targets for another 26. Iron Valiant completed seventeen of 29 passes for 157 yards, with two touchdowns and no interceptions. The Pride finished with 244 total yards. They were competitive enough to lead, then competitive enough to make Mt. Silver finish the game properly after losing that lead.
The last recovery belonged to the quarterback

Blaziken supplied both Reds sacks, for losses of seven and eight yards. The second came with 2:14 left in the fourth quarter, on the possession Petalburg was using to chase a ten-point deficit. The Pride kept going. On fourth-and-five at the two-minute mark, Iron Valiant threw short left to Girafarig for a fourteen-yard touchdown. The extra point made it 17–14. A comfortable ending had disappeared.

Porygon-Z recovered Sunflora’s onside kick. That is an unusual sentence to place near the center of a quarterback’s afternoon, but it was a vital piece of this one. Petalburg needed the ball back, and Mt. Silver kept it. Vibrava then contributed a ten-yard run left and a twelve-yard reception short left before Porygon-Z took the final kneels. The offense that had been scoreless for half the game handled the closing responsibility.

Petalburg lost one fumble, on Whiscash’s three-yard reception with 28 seconds remaining in the second quarter; Mienfoo recovered it. Mt. Silver did not turn that chance into points before the break. The Reds lost no fumbles and threw no interceptions themselves. The difference mattered over the full afternoon even when an individual recovery did not immediately improve the scoreboard.

The injury report still leaves McLarren with substantial work: Alakazam is out for the season, Lynch has four weeks remaining, and the Reds have Snowpoint next. Petalburg falls to 5–2 and goes into its bye with a narrow loss to an unbeaten opponent. Neither team needs an exaggerated lesson from three points. The Reds have earned seven wins; the Pride made this one difficult enough to be worth remembering.

For Mt. Silver, the clearest memory may be the quarterback holding an onside kick while his team protected a three-point lead. There was still a run, a pass and two kneels to complete. Porygon-Z and the Reds completed them.

art.alt: Mt. Silver quarterback Porygon-Z No. 8 in red and silver.

articles.title: Rustboro owned the yardage. Vivillon took the lead.
articles.dek: Azalea erased a 10–0 halftime deficit, won on a 50-yard pass and stopped Rustboro’s last fourth down to claim a 14–10 comeback.
articles.author: rowan-vale

body.text: Rustboro accumulated 334 yards, nineteen first downs and plenty of material for an extremely unconvincing explanation of why it lost. Azalea accumulated the final fourteen points. Vivillon’s fifty-yard touchdown catch with 2:38 remaining put the Swarm ahead, and Kricketune’s stop on fourth-and-five preserved a 14–10 victory. There is a reason the largest numbers in the game report are printed beside the team names.

The Stone led 10–0 at halftime and did not score again. Their first three possessions traveled 76, 64 and 69 yards. Those drives produced a touchdown, a field goal and a lost fumble. Azalea had almost no margin for another early concession, and Crabrawler’s recovery near the end of the half kept the comeback small enough to remain practical. Rustboro had done a great deal of work without making the game safe.

Philly supplied the first touchdown, running up the middle for three yards on third-and-one with 1:43 left in the opening quarter. Gorebyss added the extra point, then a 31-yard field goal with 2:57 remaining in the second. The Stone were moving the ball patiently and repeatedly. At that stage, another scoring drive looked more plausible than a second half in which none of them would pay off.
The yards were there. I’m not going to argue with the part where we needed more points. Keeping the ball at the end of that run would have helped us do that.
body.speaker: My Way, Son

body.text: My Way, Son ran for 109 yards on eighteen carries, a useful afternoon by almost every conventional rushing measure. With 23 seconds left before halftime, however, the Iron Treads gained nine yards on a run left and fumbled. Crabrawler recovered for Azalea. Last week, two 94-yard kickoff touchdowns had helped make My Way, Son the story of Rustboro’s win at Dewford. This week the decisive special contribution was missing, and one ordinary rushing mistake carried a much larger bill.
The comeback took two different routes

Azalea did not immediately transform the reprieve into a smooth offense. Its first possession after halftime covered 72 yards and ended on downs. Rustboro’s defense had protected the ten-point lead through another long drive. The Swarm had to get the ball back and begin again, which is less convenient than the usual comeback montage but considerably closer to what happened.

Zoroark helped by sacking Porygon-Z for five yards at 3:20 in the third quarter. Rustboro punted after gaining only two yards on that possession. Azalea’s next drive traveled forty yards and finished with Mienfoo running up the middle for a fifteen-yard touchdown on third-and-two, with eighteen seconds remaining in the quarter. Sunflora’s extra point cut the lead to 10–7. Now the Stone’s lost opportunities had a visible price.

Mienfoo carried only twice, for 22 yards. Beedrill handled the larger rushing workload, twelve carries for 56. The contrast is useful: Azalea needed its regular gains, and it also needed the less frequent runner to finish a particular chance. The Swarm produced 84 rushing yards overall, well behind Rustboro’s 150. They used one of those runs to put seven points on the board when the game was beginning to run out.

Rustboro then drove 53 yards and turned the ball over on downs. Azalea took over and moved 75 yards in five plays. The final fifty came when Drampa threw deep right to Vivillon with 2:38 left. It was the only touchdown pass of the game, and it changed the leader. Sunflora’s extra point made it 14–10. The Swarm had spent most of the afternoon chasing; now Rustboro needed a touchdown.
I knew we needed the catch. Once it was mine, I wanted the whole play. There wasn’t much to say afterward. I was looking at the score.
body.speaker: Vivillon

body.text: Vivillon finished with four catches on six targets for 96 yards. Drampa completed twelve of 22 passes for 176 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. Those are not the numbers of an offense that dominated every exchange. They are the numbers of an offense that stayed close enough for its best passing play to decide the lead. Bugsy’s team had given itself one good opportunity to make a dramatic fact out of a fairly modest passing day.
The Stone had one more long drive

Rustboro’s final possession again made progress. On third-and-eleven with 1:56 remaining, Porygon-Z found Gengar deep right for 25 yards. Lombre later caught a six-yard pass short right. Watchog converted a fourth-and-one with a run up the middle. The Stone kept extending the argument, and Azalea kept being required to answer another snap. A team can lose this kind of game by assuming the previous good stop was the last one it needed.

With 1:02 left, Rustboro faced fourth-and-five. My Way, Son ran left and gained nothing; Kricketune made the tackle. That was the end of the Stone’s last scoring opportunity. Azalea still needed to close the game, and Drampa’s fifteen-yard completion short right to Hippopotas with 57 seconds remaining helped provide the final answer before a kneel. The Swarm had won both the explosive-play contest and the last necessary small exchange.

Gengar caught five passes for eighty yards for Rustboro. Porygon-Z completed eighteen of 32 for 184 yards, without a touchdown or an interception. The Stone converted six of twelve third downs and ran 64 plays to Azalea’s forty. Tyler Scarboro has enough evidence of movement here to resist declaring the whole offense broken. He also has a second-half zero that will not improve by being surrounded with favorable statistics.

Both clubs are now 3–4. Rustboro visits Viridian next; Azalea hosts Cianwood. The Swarm will have to account for Scraggy’s two-week absence after a game in which he recorded a sack. Rustboro still has Parasect unavailable for four weeks. Those are next week’s problems. This week ended when a team with more yards needed five more and Kricketune allowed none.

art.alt: Azalea receiver Vivillon No. 11 with a football.
